g.title: delivery
g.text: 1 · Delivery — how a commit becomes running infrastructure
the main branch is the only durable state; everything below is derived from it

g.title: cluster_author
g.text: Authoring, and what guards the merge

g.title: cluster_sites
g.text: The same pipeline lands in three clusters

g.title: a_change
g.text: a human, or a pi build agent driven by

g.title: a_gate
g.text: Local gate — must pass before commit
tools/check.sh — CI-pinned render of all three clusters

g.title: a_ci
g.text: a render matrix posts a sticky rendered-diff
comment per cluster, alongside the YAML,

g.title: g_repo
g.text: THE MAIN BRANCH IS THE ONLY DURABLE STATE.
Nothing is real until it is committed and reconciled.

g.title: a_renovate
g.text: grouped per cluster per subsystem, so that
two sites never roll the same component at once

g.title: f_src
g.text: an ignore filter admits only the paths that site
and kubernetes/, plus a couple of extras at two
Only Ottawa authenticates — the other two fetch

g.title: f_sops
g.text: PGP, with the private key held in-cluster
encrypts only data and stringData in *.sops.yaml

g.title: f_ks
g.text: cluster — this cluster's own Flux config and vars

g.title: f_subst
g.text: kubernetes-apps patches this into every child,
and it is the whole reason one base directory
Substitution is SINGLE PASS: a $ inside a
substituted value is not expanded again.

g.title: f_pointer
g.text: THE EXISTENCE OF THIS FILE IS THE DEPLOY DECISION.
An app in base with no pointer anywhere is not
deployed. metadata.name is the app identity.
Carries any dependsOn, wait and timeout.

g.title: f_notify
g.text: Providers and Alerts, plus a GitHub commit

g.title: o_upstream
g.text: Helm, OCI and Git sources, every one of them

g.title: f_base
g.text: the real manifests, written exactly once
split into <app>-<location> only when the config
genuinely differs, never merely to reorder keys

g.title: o_foreign
g.text: Three apps are not delivered from this repo
bhaiya — its own GitRepository pointing at a
self-hosted Forgejo, with a Flux Receiver so that
a push triggers a reconcile without waiting for
firecrawl — straight from the upstream project
AND Robbinsdale; only its config lives here, so an
upstream bump needs no commit in this repo

g.title: o_bootstrap
g.text: controllers. After that, the cluster's own Flux
config takes over and Flux manages itself.

g.title: s_note
g.text: What each cluster actually ends up running
is listed in docs/reference/inventory.md — every machine,
namespace and Flux Kustomization, generated from this tree
by tools/gen-inventory.sh, so it cannot disagree with it.
